key_insight: Photovoltaics look strongly net-positive at the panel level, but their energy return drops sharply once reliable, always-available electricity delivery is included.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that grid integration, storage, overbuild, and backup requirements can dominate system-level net energy and emissions, so firming strategy is a core design constraint for low-carbon power systems.
method: Includes component turnover, grids, storage, overbuild, dispatchable backup, and fuel supply
Compares unfirmed renewables with battery, hydrogen, and gas firming scenarios
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark EROI ranges and GWP100 intensities across firming options in an illustrative Central European wind-PV mix, using an accounting framework rather than a predictive simulation.
watch_item: The results are illustrative benchmark values with favorable assumptions set to unity, so real deployments will typically have lower EROI and higher emissions.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
